probe: Can deterministic effect-resource identity using standard HTTP PUT plus If-None-Match:* eliminate idempotency-key retention when the useful effect is exactly the addressed resource state, and where do hidden or non-resource side effects invalidate the equivalence?

public_sources.qualification: RFC 9110 section 9.2.2 defines PUT as idempotent in intended effect while explicitly allowing separate non-idempotent side effects such as logging or revision history.
RFC 9110 section 9.3.4 defines PUT as creating or replacing the target resource state and notes that PUT can have side effects on other resources.
RFC 9110 section 13.1.2 requires If-None-Match:* to be evaluated before the method and requires 412 without performing the method when a current representation exists.

tested_scope: Documentation-level architectural falsification using only the frozen CLEAN root/config, own role-local state, and RFC 9110. No external effect, O/downstream/other-worker semantics, protected authority, hosted compute, paid/trial API, manual execution, or quota-bearing service was used.
semantic_conclusion: When the complete useful effect is exactly the durable state of a client-known stable target resource, PUT to a deterministic effect URI with If-None-Match:* can remove a separate idempotency-key retention table: the resource identity itself is the durable duplicate key, and a retry after an ambiguous successful create is rejected with 412 before the method runs while the representation exists. This equivalence is conditional, not general. It fails if the target representation can disappear before retries are impossible, if the useful effect is not fully represented by that resource state, or if hidden/non-resource side effects can occur without being transactionally coupled to the successful durable resource creation. HTTP idempotence constrains intended requested effect, not every implementation side effect; PUT may affect other resources. Therefore a charge, email, queue enqueue, append, or other hidden effect cannot inherit duplicate safety merely because the request method is PUT. A persistent immutable/tombstoned effect resource plus atomic coupling is required if those effects are to be covered.
falsification_boundaries: If a duplicate arrives while the deterministic resource has a current representation, RFC 9110 requires the If-None-Match:* precondition to block method execution; this supports exact-resource duplicate safety.

If that representation is deleted or garbage-collected before the retry horizon closes, the same duplicate can again satisfy If-None-Match:* and recreate the effect; retention dependence has only moved into resource/tombstone lifetime.

If an attempt performs a hidden effect but fails before durably creating the target representation, a retry can repeat the hidden effect because no representation exists to make the precondition false.

If the intended useful outcome includes non-resource effects not atomically bound to resource creation, PUT idempotence alone is insufficient because RFC 9110 permits non-idempotent side effects outside the requested intended effect.

frontier: r259 established the atomic sink-idempotency boundary for external duplicate safety.
r260 showed full response replay can weaken to durable completion evidence plus authoritative read under atomic identity/effect binding.
r261 shows a separate idempotency-key registry can be eliminated when deterministic resource identity itself persists and exactly represents the useful effect.
Resource deletion/expiry reintroduces a retention horizon; persistent tombstones or immutable identities are needed for retries beyond live-resource lifetime.
Hidden/non-resource side effects require atomic coupling to durable resource creation; PUT method idempotence alone does not cover them.
